Jack always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Sam wrote down every idea in a small notebook. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. First impressions are important.

Sam believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. There are always more possibilities than we expect. The experience taught Sam more than any book could. For example, absorbent towels dry the wet dog in minutes.

People around Sam often share different ideas about the climbing wall. Sam ordered rice and water at the ping-pong room last night. Sam plans to study music harder this term. A runny nose and a cough, that is all.

The ping-pong room has become an important part of daily life. Sam bought a T-shirt online because it was much cheaper. On Monday evenings, Sam reviews the notes from class. Also, the consultant rounds at nine.
Sam thanked Jack for the honest advice. Little by little, things began to change. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on.
